title.narrative: Strengthening national capacity for implementing the enhanced transparency framework in Cook Islands

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The Cook Islands Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT) project will deliver significant socioeconomic benefits at both national and local levels. Nationally, the project will enhance the capacity of government institutions responsible for climate data collection, analysis, and reporting, leading to better-informed policy decisions and more effective climate mitigation and adaptation strategies. Improved coordination among various government ministries and agencies will also reduce redundancies and improve resource efficiency, benefiting the national economy. Furthermore, building capacity and enhancing the skills of relevant stakeholders creates opportunities for job growth and economic development.At the local level, the project will empower communities by involving them in climate reporting and data collection processes. Local stakeholders, including women’s groups, community organizations, and the private sector, will participate in capacity-building workshops and training sessions, enhancing their understanding of climate change issues and equipping them with the skills needed to contribute to national climate goals. Accurate climate data will inform more effective and targeted adaptation measures, protecting livelihoods, enhancing food security, and reducing the risk of climate-related disasters.The socioeconomic benefits of the CBIT project will also support global environmental and adaptation goals. By improving the accuracy of GHG inventories and tracking NDC implementation, the project contributes to global efforts to mitigate climate change. Enhanced climate data management and reporting will enable the Cook Islands to implement effective adaptation strategies, reducing vulnerability to climate-related hazards and ensuring sustainable development. Beneficiaries include government institutions, local communities, the private sector, and NGOs, all of whom will be better equipped to participate in and benefit from climate action initiatives.
